inspected.title: NeuroBench: A Framework for Benchmarking Neuromorphic Computing Algorithms and Systems
inspected.leadAuthors: Jason Yik, Korneel Van den Berghe, Douwe den Blanken and 97 further authors
inspected.identityCheck: Title, arXiv identifier, author list and version confirmed from the abstract page before the full text was read.
inspected.rightsBasis: Open access on arXiv. Retrieved without circumventing any access control.
exactLocators: Algorithm Track Metrics, under Algorithm Track Benchmark Framework
Algorithm Track Limitations and Further Extensions

observedDefinitions.verbatim: Memory footprint, in bytes, required to represent a model
Number of zero weights divided by the total number of weights
Average sparsity of neuron activations over all neurons in all model layers
All zero and nonzero neuron activations and synaptic connections
Effective multiply-accumulate operations, disregarding zero activations and connections
Task-specific metrics including accuracy, mean average precision, R-squared and sMAPE

statedLimitations: Metrics are restricted to digital, time-stepped algorithm execution; analog and continuous-time deployment is undefined.
Synaptic operations does not account for neuron updates.
Data pre- and post-processing can amount to significant costs not captured by these metrics.
Model Execution Rate is not well defined for event-based or continuous-time contexts.
inspected.boundary: Defines how to report and compare submitted neuromorphic systems. It does not establish that any system is faster, more efficient or more biologically realistic than another, and by its own statement does not capture neuron updates or data processing costs.

exactLocators: Document Analysis, the four named stages
inspected.observedContent: Prescribes a four-stage progression: Meet the document. Observe its parts. Try to make sense of it. Use it as historical evidence.
inspected.boundary: Establishes that a national archive publishes a staged document-analysis method. It does not establish that any other three-step formulation is that method, and it makes no claim about religious texts specifically.
